findings.asked: Surface area of a cylinder, then the force from its pressure on the floor.
findings.wentWrong: Many confused surface area with volume; a third got part (a); few connected area, pressure and force, and many fed their part (a) answer into part (b).
findings.rule: Force = pressure x area of the face touching the floor.

findings.asked: Volume of a cylinder, then the force it exerts on the floor.
findings.wentWrong: The volume was fine (some used r = 12 for a diameter of 12); many used that volume in the force calculation, and some missed the rounding instruction.
findings.rule: Pressure uses the contact area, never the volume.

findings.asked: Equal pressures from two solids; find the base edge of a square-based pyramid.
findings.wentWrong: Many got the cube's pressure but then divided the force by a length, a volume or a surface area (5, 125, 150) instead of the base area; those who reached the area often divided by 4 rather than square-rooting to get the edge.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Pressure = 560 / (base area of the cube), set equal to force / base area of the pyramid, solved for the area, then square-rooted.
findings.rule: Side of a square = square root of its area.

findings.asked: The same pressure problem on M4.
findings.wentWrong: Many started with the cube's volume and scored nothing; the final step of dividing by four instead of square-rooting recurred. The report's diagnosis: too much focus on the formula, too little on which area is in contact.
findings.rule: Write 'area in contact = ...' before you use the formula.

ruleToRemember: Pressure = force / area of the face in contact; state which face and its area before calculating; a square's side is the square root of its area.
aStarSignal: Equating two pressures to find an unknown dimension, with the contact areas named explicitly.
